title: Sleeping capacity before permanent bedrooms
applies_when: Colonists lack usable sleeping capacity or current sleeping construction is stalled.
approach: Count existing and pending capacity before adding more. Separate a place to sleep from enclosure, roof and comfort.
Compare temporary zero-cost sleeping places with constructed beds using native definition costs and work. An interim place can be useful while durable furniture is built.
Reuse suitable existing space when observed; choose expansion sites from actual nearby geometry rather than a sampled room cell.

For a humanlike sleeping-capacity construction objective, set definition_requirements to is_bed=true and bed_humanlike=true. The executor must check these native properties; do not select animal beds.
verify: Current colonist count, existing beds/spots, ownership and reachability.
Native footprint, costs, roofs, door access and construction work blockers.
For colonist sleeping capacity, inspect native is_bed and bed_humanlike. Animal beds do not provide humanlike sleeping capacity. Match the intended users before choosing material or position.
reconsider: Existing capacity already meets the objective.
Chosen space is inaccessible, unsafe or conflicts with player direction.
